Growth Chamber (GC) Soybean Transpiration Analysis

PI: Elvis F. Elli · University of Arkansas  |  Project: RIG 2024–2026  |  Report generated: 2026-05-21

Three growth chamber experiments testing VPD-response in soybean accessions classified by WUE plasticity (Chamarthi et al. 2022). Primary response variable: transpiration per unit leaf area (mg m⁻² s⁻¹), measured as pot weight loss over a 40-min treatment window normalised by leaf area. Relative transpiration (0–1) retained for cross-experiment comparison.

2. Methods & QC

Transpiration measurement

Pots were weighed at the beginning and end of each 40-min VPD treatment window. Weight loss (g ≈ ml) = water transpired. Three weighings were taken per treatment; values are averaged before computing transpiration (as in the processed spreadsheets).

Transpiration per leaf area (mg m⁻² s⁻¹) = Transpiration (ml) × 1000 / leaf area (m²) / 2400 s.

Relative transpiration = Transpiration(Ti) / max(Transpiration) per pot and day, normalised so the treatment with maximum weight loss = 1.0.

VPD treatments

  • GC1 & GC2: 6 levels, target RH = 80, 68, 56, 44, 32, 20% at 32°C
  • GC3: 5 levels, target RH = 80, 68, 56, 44, 32% at 32°C
  • Actual VPD measured from chamber probes; values in the cleaned CSV are measured averages per treatment.

Day effect and primary analysis day

Day 2 is used for all primary analysis. Day 1 shows a systematic acclimation artifact: plants not yet at equilibrium after transitioning from growth conditions to the measurement protocol. GC1 and GC3 show Day 1 mean relative transpiration 10–30% below Day 2. GC2 shows a smaller Day effect (plants may have been closer to equilibrium). All figures and statistics below use Day 2 unless stated otherwise.

Outlier detection

Outliers defined as observations > 2.5 SD from the genotype × treatment group mean (within each experiment, Day 2 only). Flagged values excluded from summary statistics and figures; raw data retained in GC_combined_clean.csv.

4. GC2 Results

GC2 tested a second set of four genotypes (one per quadrant), 4 replications, 6 VPD levels over 2 days (Oct 30–31, 2024). Leaf area, dry matter, and transpiration per leaf area were measured.

Data note — GC2 anomaly: Pot 1, Day 1, Treatment 6 (highest VPD) recorded a net weight gain (−7.4 ml transpiration), indicating irrigation or measurement error during this window. This value is set to NA in GC2_clean.csv. All other 191 records are valid.

6. Overall / Combined Analysis

All three experiments combined: 12 genotypes, 512 observations total (Day 2 n ≈ 256). Quadrant colour coding: Q1 = orange, Q2 = teal, Q3 = purple, Q4 = pink. Experiment line style: GC1 = solid, GC2 = dashed, GC3 = dotted.

7. Key Findings

Response pattern

  • Across all three experiments, transpiration (actual and relative) increases with VPD up to approximately 2–3 kPa, consistent with the Sinclair (2008) limited-transpiration threshold framework.
  • Q1 genotypes (Plastic, High WUE — PI471938, PI398245, PI398617) tend toward a plateau or slight decline in transpiration at high VPD, consistent with a VPD-threshold response and the limited-transpiration (LT) trait.
  • Q4 genotypes (Nonplastic, High WUE) show a more linear increase with VPD across the tested range.
  • Q2 and Q3 genotypes show variable responses, with Q3 generally displaying lower overall transpiration per leaf area.

Experiment consistency

  • GC2 genotypes show somewhat higher absolute transpiration per leaf area than GC1/GC3 genotypes at equivalent VPDs, likely due to larger plant size at time of measurement (later vegetative stage).
  • Relative transpiration patterns are more consistent across experiments, supporting cross-experiment comparability.
  • The Day 1 acclimation artifact is consistent across GC1 and GC3; GC2 shows a smaller effect, possibly because plants were measured at a more advanced and stable growth stage.

8. Data Notes

File structure

FileDescription
cleaned_data/GC2_clean.csv GC2 primary analysis file extracted from Data analysis 2.xlsx Final sheet. 192 rows; one NA (Pot 1, Day 1, T6 weight-gain anomaly).
cleaned_data/GC_combined_clean.csv All three experiments combined. 512 rows × 25 columns. Primary analysis file.
raw_data/GC2/GC_experiment_2.xlsx Raw weight tracking spreadsheet (Tracking weights sheet). Source for verification.
raw_data/GC2/Data analysis 2.xlsx Processed GC2 data (transpiration per pot per treatment, leaf area, dry matter). Source for GC2_clean.csv.

GC2 data processing

GC2 was processed from the Final sheet of Data analysis 2.xlsx, which matches the format of GC3's Final sheet. One cell error was detected and corrected: Pot 1, Day 1, Treatment 2 had Transpiration_ml = 8.553 (incorrect, copy/paste error from Pot 2 T1) — corrected to 13.633 by back-calculation from TranspLeafArea × LeafArea_squarecm.

Scripts

  • scripts/GC2_process_raw.py — alternative raw-weights extraction (from Tracking weights sheet; superseded by Final sheet extraction)
  • scripts/GC_figures.py — generates all PNG figures in this report
  • scripts/GC_build_report.py — generates this HTML report
  • scripts/GC_comprehensive_analysis.R — R-based analysis (GC1 + GC3; update needed to include GC2)
